**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve unrelated canonical stashes**

When the canonical clone contains an older, unrelated, or additional stash, `git stash list` does not prove that the stashed content is present on `origin/main`, yet this diagnostic directs the operator to drop it and the accompanying workflow prescribes an unqualified `git stash drop`. Following that remediation can permanently discard non-pin work; identify and verify the specific autostash before recommending removal, while reporting other stashes for manual review.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:df21d590c8fb592306b0de61d4dfb89ea6ce237d

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject a stale HEAD when its dirty bytes match origin/main**

After the pins PR merges, running `make update` in the canonical clone fetches the new `origin/main` but deliberately skips its pull because the pin files are still modified. If those working-tree bytes exactly match the merged commit, this `git diff origin/main` is empty, so the boundary check passes even though `HEAD` remains behind and `git status` is dirty; the clone then stays unable to update normally and a later upgrade starts from stale repository state. Require the canonical checkout itself to be clean and its `HEAD` to match the comparison ref after reconciliation, rather than accepting byte equality alone.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify tree entries instead of working-tree file hashes**

When an upgrade changes a tracked symlink, deletes a file, or changes only its executable mode, this blob-identity procedure is incomplete: `git hash-object <file>` follows a symlink and hashes its target contents, fails for a deleted path, and does not encode the mode, while `git rev-parse <head>:<file>` reads the committed blob and likewise cannot verify mode changes. Consequently, valid symlink/deletion updates cannot satisfy the prescribed comparison, while a worker-side mode change can pass it unnoticed; record and compare the resulting tree entry (mode, object ID, and an explicit deletion state) for every changed path instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:df21d590c8fb592306b0de61d4dfb89ea6ce237d

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Generate full object IDs for added-file patches**

When `make upgrade` creates an untracked file, the prescribed `git diff --no-index /dev/null <file>` emits abbreviated object IDs by default, while acceptance compares its headers against `git diff --full-index <base> <head>`, which emits full IDs. As `git diff -h` states, `--full-index` is what “show[s] full object name on index lines,” so an unchanged added file will still fail this header-for-header identity check; add `--full-index` to the added-file command as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include staged pin changes in the extracted patch**

When the canonical clone contains a staged-only pin change, the prescribed `git diff --full-index -- <files>` compares the index with the working tree and emits nothing for that change; `git diff -h` exposes `--cached` as a separate staged-diff form. This is a supported state because the new boundary check explicitly detects staged-only changes and tells the operator to carry them as a pins task, but the resulting task can silently omit the staged file and still pass an empty header comparison. Diff against `HEAD` (or combine cached and unstaged patches) so the promised whole pending pin diff is transferred.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reconcile untracked additions before pulling the merged PR**

When the pins patch contains an added file, that file remains untracked in the canonical clone after the PR merges, so the documented next `git pull` aborts because the merge would overwrite an untracked path rather than creating and reapplying an autostash. `git stash push -h` confirms that untracked files require the explicit `-u/--include-untracked` option, which pull's autostash does not provide. Document a pre-pull reconciliation for added paths—such as staging/restoring them from the fetched `origin/main`—instead of claiming every merged patch becomes an autostash no-op.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run added-file diffs from the canonical clone**

When `make upgrade` creates an untracked file in the canonical clone, the orchestrator remains seated in the separate working clone, but this added-file command omits `git -C <canonical>`. `git diff -h` defines this form as `git diff ... --no-index [--] <path> <path>`, so `<file>` is resolved from the current working directory; it will usually be missing and produce no patch, or could silently read a different same-named file. Run the no-index diff from the canonical clone so the complete pins patch is transferred.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve unstaged bytes while normalizing the index**

When a pin file contains both staged and additional unstaged edits, the prescribed `git checkout -- <files>` replaces its working-tree version with the staged index version before `restore --staged` runs, permanently discarding the unstaged edits and producing an incomplete patch. `git checkout -h` identifies this invocation as the path-checkout form, `git checkout ... -- <file>...`; restrict that copy step to genuinely index-only paths, while unstaging mixed paths without overwriting their working-tree content.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:0003cbdf97b3499069e4cefbfc2f755ae0c064f1

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare added symlinks without dereferencing them**

When the pins patch adds a symlink, `git show origin/main:<file>` emits the symlink blob (its target path), but `cmp -s - <canonical>/<file>` opens and dereferences the filesystem symlink, so it compares that blob with the target file's contents and rejects a correctly merged addition. `cmp --help` confirms that it compares its file operands byte by byte. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier identity discussion is this new post-merge `cmp` check; use a symlink-aware comparison such as `readlink` or compare the tree entry before removing the untracked link.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
